text: The next day. <break time="0.8s" /> No one dared to ask him. <break time="0.8s" /> Why he wore the veil. <break time="0.8s" /> And even a deputation from the church. <break time="0.8s" /> Sat speechless before him. <break time="0.8s" /> And returned without an answer. <break time="0.8s" /> But there was one person in the village. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was not frightened by the veil. <break time="0.8s" /> And she was Elizabeth. <break time="0.8s" /> The young woman to whom he was engaged. <break time="0.8s" /> There is nothing terrible. <break time="0.8s" /> In this piece of crape. <break time="0.8s" /> She said calmly. <break time="0.8s" /> So come, good sir. <break time="0.8s" /> Let the sun shine. <break time="0.8s" /> From behind the cloud. <break time="0.8s" /> There is an hour to come. <break time="0.8s" /> When all of us shall cast aside our veils. <break time="0.8s" /> He answered. <break time="0.8s" /> So do not be offended. <break time="0.8s" /> If I wear it till then. <break time="0.8s" /> She warned him gently. <break time="0.8s" /> That people were beginning to whisper. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was hiding his face. <break time="0.8s" /> Because of some secret sin. <break time="0.8s" /> If I hide my face for sorrow. <break time="0.8s" /> There is cause enough. <break time="0.8s" /> He replied. <break time="0.8s" /> And if I cover it for secret sin. <break time="0.8s" /> What mortal might not do the same. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the terror of the veil. <break time="0.8s" /> Fell upon Elizabeth too. <break time="0.8s" /> And when he begged her. <break time="0.8s" /> Not to desert him. <break time="0.8s" /> She asked him to lift it but once. <break time="0.8s" /> Never, It cannot be he replied. <break time="0.8s" /> And Elizabeth, saying farewell. <break time="0.8s" /> Slowly departed. <break time="0.8s" /> Pausing at the door. <break time="0.8s" /> To give one long, shuddering gaze at the veil.
